extracted.intended_audience: registrants (public companies) required to file with the SEC; corporate legal, compliance, investor-relations, and audit/governance personnel; securities lawyers and investors
extracted.subtask_description: Rules and required disclosures for registrants to describe board and management oversight of material climate-related risks, and certain related disclosures (e.g., use of internal carbon pricing). Focus is on what disclosures are required, which proposed elements were modified or omitted, and how disclosures should be tailored to material risks.

rubrics_metrics.name: Internal carbon price disclosure
rubrics_metrics.description: Describe how the registrant uses an internal carbon price to evaluate and manage a material climate-related risk when responding to other final rule provisions (e.g., when describing a related transition plan).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The final rule streamlines the internal carbon price disclosure requirement: registrants should describe their use of an internal carbon price as it relates to material climate risks, but the Commission eliminated the proposed requirements to disclose (1) a separate narrative description of how the registrant uses an internal carbon price and (2) the rationale for selecting the internal carbon price applied. The disclosure is subject to the same safe harbor that applies to transition plan and scenario analysis disclosure. These changes aim to provide investors material information while limiting compliance burden and avoiding disclosure of confidential/proprietary information. The Commission also declined to adopt a special exemption, exception, or phase-in for this requirement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Board oversight disclosure (Item 1501(a)) — description of oversight
rubrics_metrics.description: Require a description of a board of directors' oversight of climate-related risks.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The final rule adopts the proposed requirement to disclose board oversight of climate-related risks in order to enhance investors' ability to evaluate management of such risks. The disclosure focuses on registrants' existing or developing governance practices and is not intended to influence board composition or operations. Disclosures are only required for registrants whose boards exercise oversight of climate-related risks (no disclosure is required if the board does not exercise oversight). The rules are intended to provide investors context to evaluate the extent to which the board is evaluating climate-related risks and to inform investment and voting decisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Identification of board committee or subcommittee responsible (Item 1501(a))
rubrics_metrics.description: If applicable, identify any board committee or subcommittee responsible for the oversight of climate-related risks.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The final rule requires identification of any committee or subcommittee tasked with managing climate-related risks. This is intended to help investors understand how the board is managing such risk and is considered not to be burdensome. The provision requires only identification of the committee/subcommittee and is not designed to influence how boards allocate responsibilities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Describe processes by which the board or committee is informed about climate-related risks
rubrics_metrics.description: Describe the processes by which the board, or any board committee/subcommittee, is informed about climate-related risks.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The final rule requires a description of the processes (but not the frequency) by which the board or committee is informed about such risks. The Commission eliminated the proposed requirement to disclose how frequently the board considers climate-related risks to avoid unduly influencing governance behavior. Retaining process-based disclosure gives investors meaningful information to assess how registrants manage material climate-related risks while avoiding overly granular disclosures that could pressure boards to change behavior.

rubrics_metrics.name: Disclosure of board oversight of targets/goals/transition plans (tied to existence of such disclosures)
rubrics_metrics.description: If a registrant has disclosed a climate-related target, goal, or transition plan pursuant to the rules, disclose whether and how the board oversees progress against that target, goal, or transition plan.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This disclosure is tied to circumstances in which the registrant has a disclosed target, goal, or transition plan (e.g., § 229.1504 or § 229.1502(e)(1)), to avoid eliciting immaterial information and reduce boilerplate. The final rule omits the proposed requirement to disclose how the board establishes targets (including interim targets), but requires description of board oversight of progress where a target/plan has been disclosed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Board disclosure elements not required / omitted
rubrics_metrics.description: The final rule does not require identification of specific board members responsible for climate-risk oversight; does not require disclosure of whether any board member has climate-related expertise or the nature of such expertise; does not require disclosure of how frequently the board is informed about climate-related risks; and does not require information about whether and how the board sets climate-related targets or goals (including interim targets).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These more prescriptive elements from the proposal were eliminated in the final rule in response to commenters' concerns that they could: (a) influence board composition or governance behavior, (b) divulge sensitive internal board processes, (c) lead to poaching or increased competition for scarce expertise, or (d) generate boilerplate or immaterial disclosures. The Commission retained flexibility so registrants may disclose such information voluntarily where appropriate, but streamlined mandatory requirements to avoid unintended adverse effects.

rubrics_metrics.name: Management oversight disclosure (Item 1501(b)) — description of role
rubrics_metrics.description: Require a description of management's role in assessing and managing material climate-related risks.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The final rule adopts the proposed requirement to describe management's role but limits it to material climate-related risks (responding to commenters' concerns about breadth). The rule aims to provide investors information about how management-level staff assess and manage material climate risks so investors can make informed investment and voting decisions. Registrants that do not exercise management oversight of material climate-related risks are not required to provide disclosures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Management positions/committees responsible and relevant expertise (Item 1501(b) non-exclusive list)
rubrics_metrics.description: Disclose, as applicable, whether and which management positions or committees are responsible for assessing and managing climate-related risks and the relevant expertise of such position holders or committee members, in such detail as necessary to fully describe the nature of the expertise.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The final rule includes this non-exclusive list item to elicit specific, non-boilerplate information regarding management oversight. The requirement to describe expertise is adopted, but limited to material risks to mitigate concerns that registrants would feel compelled to hire personnel solely to satisfy disclosure expectations. Registrants should tailor disclosure level to what is material and necessary to describe the nature of the expertise.

rubrics_metrics.name: Processes by which management assesses and manages climate-related risks
rubrics_metrics.description: Describe the processes by which the responsible management positions or committees assess and manage climate-related risks.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A process-based description is encouraged to provide investors meaningful insight into how registrants manage material climate risks while allowing flexibility to avoid overly prescriptive or burdensome reporting. This approach is intended to reduce boilerplate and accommodate varied organizational structures across registrants.

rubrics_metrics.name: Whether management reports to the board (and to whom)
rubrics_metrics.description: Disclose, as applicable, whether the management positions or committees responsible for climate-related risks report information about such risks to the board of directors or a committee/subcommittee of the board.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The final rule retains disclosure about whether management reports to the board (or a board committee/subcommittee) as an example of responsive disclosure. This helps clarify the connection between management-level and board-level governance of material climate-related risks. The Commission omitted many of the more prescriptive or granular reporting-frequency requirements from the proposal in order to avoid inducing changes in business practices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Management disclosure elements not required / omitted
rubrics_metrics.description: The final rule does not include additional proposed elements such as organizational diagrams showing reporting lines, detailed information about climate-based remuneration, or mandatory disclosure of identities that commenters argued could be proprietary or burdensome.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: While commenters suggested additional disclosures (e.g., org diagrams, compensation linkage), the Commission limited required management disclosures to a focused, materiality-limited, non-exclusive list to balance investor information needs against burdens and potential competitive harm. Registrants may voluntarily include additional information (e.g., climate-related opportunities) but such disclosures are optional.

rubrics_metrics.name: Materiality scope for management disclosures
rubrics_metrics.description: Management oversight disclosures are required only with respect to material climate-related risks.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The final rule incorporates a materiality qualifier for management-level disclosures to limit burden and to allow registrants to tailor disclosures to those climate matters that are material to their business. This addresses concerns about producing excessive or immaterial information, especially for smaller registrants or registrants without formalized internal controls for such disclosures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Treatment of climate-related opportunities disclosures
rubrics_metrics.description: Disclosure regarding management's role in assessing and managing climate-related opportunities is optional (registrants may elect to include such disclosure but it is not mandatory).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Commission decided not to require disclosures about climate-related opportunities to avoid anti-competitive concerns and to keep voluntary disclosures available. Some commenters urged mandatory disclosure to align with EU/UK practices, but the SEC treated opportunity disclosures as voluntary to mitigate concerns about competitive harm and one-size-fits-all governance approaches.

rubrics_metrics.name: Overarching principle: disclosure focus and non-prescriptiveness
rubrics_metrics.description: The final rules focus on disclosure of existing oversight practices and do not seek to influence registrants' decisions about governance structure or to mandate specific board composition or management structures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Commission emphasized that the rules are designed to improve investor access to comparable, decision-useful information while avoiding design choices that would pressure companies to change governance practices. The approach is intentionally less prescriptive than the proposal to reduce risk of boilerplate, protect confidential processes, and avoid elevating climate governance above other disclosure areas. Registrants have flexibility to determine the level of detail to provide about board and management oversight consistent with whether the board/management exercises oversight and the materiality of the risks.
